new_statements.quote: We have identified five surface tones in Mfumte: three level tones: high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]; and two contour tones, rising [ǎ] and falling [â]. [p. 8] ... There are no long vowels in Mfumte, no nasal vowels and because of the use of the labial glide w and the palatal glide y, there are no diphthongs. [p. 7] ... Though each village has its own place of origin with its own distinct manner of speaking, they have all agreed to be treated as a dialect cluster with Lus as the standard. [p. 1]

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given anywhere. The language (Lus variety) is described as a tone language with three level and two contour surface tones, lexically contrastive (minimal pairs for H/M/L, rising, falling); mid tone is left unmarked in the orthography. The words 'stress', 'accent' and 'prominence' do not occur in the guide, in McLean's 2014 sketch grammar (which says only 'Surface tone markings are used and no formal attempt has been made to account for tonal alternation', p. 9, and 'the role of tone in Central Mfumte grammar remains to be fully researched', p. 34), or in the two SIL surveys.
new_statements.exceptions: None; falling tones are said to be concentrated on the prefix /mâ-/ and on the second syllable of reduplicated roots (p. 8); rising tone marks plural on monosyllabic low-toned nouns and hortative/imperative verb forms (p. 8; McLean 2014:13).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone in citation forms; nouns are mostly monosyllabic stems (McLean 2014:9); no statement about stress at word or phrase level. Describes Lus = Central Mfumte (cent2312), not the Koffa/Southern group.
new_statements.identity_note: Every phonological description that exists is of the Lus village variety, which Glottolog 5.3 files as a separate language, Central Mfumte (cent2312), sister of Southern Mfumte (mfum1238) under Central-Southern Mfumte (cent2313); both share ISO code nfu because the 2017 split request (ISO CR 2017-006) was rejected. Southern Mfumte proper = the Koffa group (Koffa koff1238, Mbat, Jui, Manang, Mbibji, Bang, Kom, Mballa, Mbah) plus Nigerian Fum (fumm1238, Blench 1999). Glottolog lists zero descriptive references for mfum1238 and assigns McLean 2014 to cent2312; PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory 1601 'Southern Mfumte' is nevertheless built from Eyoh & Hedinger 2008 (Lus data) via the ISO code.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2017. Change Request 2017-006 (submitter Greg McLean): split [nfu] into Southern Mfumte and Central Mfumte — rejected 2018-01-23.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; establishes that Koffa (Southern) and Lus (Central) are separate development projects and that Lus materials are not usable in the western/southern villages.

sources.citation: McLean, Greg L. 2015. A Recorded Text Survey of the Mfumte Speech Varieties and Rapid Appraisal Survey of Dzodinka. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2015-004. Dallas: SIL International. 54 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (RTT with Koffa, Lus, Kwaja stories; RA of Adere); no phonology, no tone or stress. p. 5: only phonology is Eyoh 2008 (Lus); p. 22 recommends for Koffa/Kwaja/Adere 'Collect a 1700-item wordlist, complete a phonology, and write a tentative orthography statement'. Via the Internet Archive 2025-02-23.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, search results for Mfumte / nfu (the Internet Archive 2015-09-17)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 6 items (Eyoh & Hedinger 2008; 2007 primer; Grant et al. 1994; Michael 2013 anthropology; McLean 2014; McLean 2015). SIL holds no phonology for nfu.

sources.citation: McLean, Greg L. 2014. A Sketch Grammar of the Central Mfumte Language. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 35 pp.
sources.note: No phonology chapter; nothing on stress. p. 9: 'Surface tone markings are used and no formal attempt has been made to account for tonal alternation'; nouns mostly monosyllabic, no noun-class system, plural by floating H tone; p. 34: 'the role of tone in Central Mfumte grammar remains to be fully researched'. p. 35 cites Eyoh 2008 phonology (DEA thesis). Obtained via Internet Archive copy 2023-12-08 of the sil.org PDF (sil.org itself is behind an automated-access block).
